FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Automotive Braking Systems Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard is one in the series of Indian Standards being developed for air brake components. 
It is an adjunct to the IS 11852 series of standards specified for the performance requirements of 
braking systems for automotive vehicles. 

Unloader valves control the delivery of air into the reservoir to limit the reservoir pressure 
between the specified lower and upper limits. It may also provide a connection for tyre inflation 
with the location agreed to between the suppliers and the purchasers. Some typical tests have 
been specified for the valves. It however does not preclude any other tests agreed to between 
the manufacturers and the purchasers such as casing integrity, water spray tests, etc. 

In the preparation of this standard assistance has also been derived from SAE J 1409 : 1988 Air 
Brake Valve Test Procedure issued by Society of Automotive Engineers, USA. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )'• 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard.

AUTOMOTIVE VEHICLES — AIR BRAKE 

SYSTEMS — PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 

FOR UNLOADER VALVES 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the performance require- 
ments, installation dimensions and tests for 
unloader valves used in automotive air brake 
systems. 

2 REFERENCE 

IS 9844: 1981 'Methods of testing corrosion 
resistance of electroplated and anodized 



aluminium coatings by neutral salt spray test' 
is a necessary adjunct to this standard.

shown in Fig. 1. The valve shall be designed to 
fit within the space indicated in the Pig. 1. The 
location for tyre infiator connection other than 
that indicated in the figure shall be agreed to 
between the manufacturers and the purchasers.

4 TESTS 

4.1 The following tests shall be carried out on 
the specimen: 

a) Leak test, 

b) Output performance test, 

c) Endurance test, 

d) Low temperature test 

e) Dry heat test, 

f) Salt spray test, 

g) Over pressure test, 
h) Relief pressure test, 
j) Vibration test, and 
k) Thread integrity test 



4.2 Working Conditions

4.3 Leak Test 



Line ( normal ) 
Mounting holes 
( optional ) 

As per pur- 
chaser's speci- 
fication 



The unit shall be checked for leaks at cut-out 
and cut-in pressures. The maximum admissible 
leak rate shall be 100 cc/min. 

4.4 Output Performance Test 

After leak test, the cut-out and cut-in pressures 
of the valve shall be checked. The pressure 
differential ( difference between cut-out and 
cut-in pressures ) shall be between 0-5 bar 
minimum and 1*4 bar maximum or 20 percent 
of cut-out pressure, whichever is higher. The 
measured cut-out pressure shall be within 
± 0-25 bar of the specified value. 



4.5 Endurance Test 

The unit shall be subjected to an endurance 
test under the following conditions: 

Total number : 2.5 x 10 5 
of cycles 

One cycle : One cut-out and one cut-in 

Frequency : 15 cycles per minute 

Stroke : 75 percent of maximum 

stroke 

In addition the tyre inflator shall be operated 
1 000 times. At the end of the test the unit 
shall be checked for performance and leakage. 
The maximum admissible leak rate shall be 250 
cc/min. The maximum variations in the cut- 
out and differential pressure shall be 0-5 bar. 

4.5.1 The performance variation after endurance 
test shall be within ± 10 percent of initial 
value . 

4.5.2 Structural Integrity Test 

Number of 10 e 

cycles 

Pressure to 8 bar 

Stroke 75 percent of maximum 

stroke 

At the end of the test there shall be no per- 
manent damage. 

4.6 Low Temperature Test 

The unit shall be kept in a chamber maintained 
at a temperature of - 25°C for 16 h. At the 
end of the test the unit shall be checked for 
performance and leakage. 

The maximum permissible variation in the cut- 
out and differential pressures shall be 0*5 bar. 

4.7 Dry Heat Test 

The unit is kept in a chamber maintained at a 
temperature of 100°C for 16 h. At the end of 
the period, the unit shall be checked for per- 
formance and leakage. The maximum admissible 
leak rate shall be 250 cc/min. The maximum 
permissible variation in the cut-out and 
differential pressure shall be 0-5 bar. 

4.8 Salt Spray Test 

The component parts shall be subjected to a 
salt spray test for 48 h as per IS 9844 : 1981. 
There shall be no corrosion of parent material 
at the end of this test. 

4.9 Over Pressure Test 

The unit shall be subjected to an air pressure 
of 10 bar for ten seconds from the inlet by 



IS 13494 : 1992 



using the tyre inflator. The unit is then sub- 
jected to 11*5 bar from the delivery for ten 
seconds. At the end of the test the unit shall 
be checked for performance and leakage. 

The maximum admissible leak rate shall be 250 
cc/min. The maximum permissible variation 
in cut-out and differential pressure shall be 
0-5 bar. 

4.10 Relief Pressure Test 

The unit shall be checked at 12 ± 2 bar relief 
pressure by suitably blocking the feedback port 
at the outlet. 



4.11 Vibration Test 

The unit shall be subjected to a vibration of 
± 5 g at 50 Hz for 10 8 cycles. 

At the end of test there shall be no structural 
failure and the unit shall be checked for per- 
formance and leak. The maximum admissible 
leak rate shall be 250 cc/min. The maximum 
permissible variations in the cut-out and 
differential pressures shall be 0-5 bar. 

4.12 Thread Integrity Test 

All threaded posts shall be checked for thread 
strength integrity by alternately tightening and 
loosening for 25 times with a specified torque. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark 
on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system 
of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and 
operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by 
BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act \ 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization* marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

or grade designation. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director
